claim.text: By the end of this year, the deficit will be down to less than half what it was before I took office.
claim.context: And tonight, I’m announcing that the Justice Department will name a chief prosecutor for pandemic fraud. || By the end of this year, the deficit will be down to less than half what it was before I took office. || The only president ever to cut the deficit by more than one trillion dollars in a single year.

row.reasoning: CBO projections and YTD FY2022 data at claim time tracked the deficit below half the $3.1T FY2020 / $2.77T FY2021 pre-Biden baselines.

evidence.snippet: [2022-03-08] CBO: FY2022 deficit just $259B in first 4 months, far below prior years — tracking toward a steep full-year drop.
[2022-03-08] CBO monthly review: FY2022 first five-month deficit $475B — less than half the same period in FY2021 ($1,047B).
[2020-11-09] Official CBO report: FY2020 deficit $3.1 trillion (pre-Biden baseline).
[2021-07-21] CBO's standing projection at claim time: FY2022 deficit ~$1.2T, below half of the FY2020/FY2021 shortfalls.
[2022-01-26] CBO report showing actual FY2021 deficit was $2.78 trillion (useful baseline for ‘before I took office’).
[2021-02-11] CBO baseline outlook projecting deficits through FY2031, available pre-claim.
[2021-10-22] Treasury/OMB: FY2021 deficit was $2.77T — the prior-year baseline against which the halving is measured.
[2021-07-01] July 2021 CBO update to 2021-2031 outlook with FY2022 projections.
Treasury FiscalData historical deficit series including FY2020.
[2022-02-08] CBO January 2022 review shows FY2022 deficit running well below prior-year pace as COVID spending wanes.
